<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 81 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ccdad23f956f725f41288599a515c81042fd7f35` — the merge of head `667a89f4d5d0b4a31a69afae35042a0b68188c61` into base `020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ccdad23f956f725f41288599a515c81042fd7f35 && git checkout ccdad23f956f725f41288599a515c81042fd7f35
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70 667a89f4d5d0b4a31a69afae35042a0b68188c61 && git checkout -B drift-repro 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70 && git merge --no-ff 667a89f4d5d0b4a31a69afae35042a0b68188c61

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cyrFFk86Jqf7Mp5Rzw
Request: review · area E2 · head 793d8251b23579fd3f5a00d223a4e20373e37b15

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `793d8251b23579fd3f5a00d223a4e20373e37b15`
Local-runs: none

Read: the PR's four commits on top of `4bba8b8f` (`c23e4055`, `0a2c2b5d`, `0305fd3b`, `793d8251`): 8 files, +439/−2. I compared the new unbind with the binder's teardown in `packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts`, read every caller of `removeActionsByPackage` and of `listRegisteredActions()` at this head, and traced the rewritten pin through its history on GitHub (#24526, #31737, #32213). I ran nothing locally.

### ① Derived judgments

**The unbind is the binder's own teardown, applied to the same owners.**
- *Same owners.* The binder tears down `owner`, `previous.owners` and the owners it binds now, and records those owners for the next bind (`app-artifact-handlers.ts:336-372`). The unbind tears down `owner` plus `previousBind(ql, owner).owners` (`:589`). That is exactly the set the last bind registered under, because `recordBind` stores the owners the bind was about to bind.
- *Same verbs.* For each owner it calls `removeActionsByPackage`, `unregisterHooksByPackage`, `unregisterFunctionsByPackage` and `releaseFunctionClaims` (`:592-598`). These are the binder's teardown verbs. The only other engine calls the binder makes are `bindHooks` and `registerAction` under the same owners, so nothing the bind registered is left behind. Jobs leave through the existing `runtime.package-jobs` cleanup, as the PR says.
- *Nothing of another holder.* Every verb removes by the exact owner string `app:<id>`. `removeActionsByPackage` drops only stack entries whose `package` equals that string (`engine-actions.ts:447-453`), so an override that another package or the environment bound over B's handler stays, with nothing beneath it. Host code is coordinate `(host)`, the environment's resync is `metadata-service` (coordinate `''`), and a plugin is its own name. None of them can equal `app:<manifestId>`.
- *Idempotent.* The unbind deletes the bind record (`:607`). A second call reads `NO_BIND`, so it tears down only `owner`, which no longer holds anything. Every verb is then a no-op, and so is the hand-back loop, because no key empties.
- *Ordered after a successful withdrawal.* `if (!withdrawal) await this.unbindArtifactHandlers(...)` (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3705`) sits after `withdrawFromRunningKernel`. It never runs on a refused withdrawal, and never on the earlier `assertPackageUninstallable` 409 or a ledger write failure, which both return before it. It runs before the `metadata:reloaded` announcement, so the authored-action resync that follows sees an engine without B. The new `await` comes after the withdrawal, so the no-await window between the ledger removal and the withdrawal is unchanged.

**The rewritten pin pinned behaviour from before ADR-0150. It was not an ADR-0150 rule.**
- The pin `withdrawing the replacing owner leaves the key with no handler — the consequence the warning names` came in with #24526 (`de43524606`, 2026-10-19). At that time there was one handler slot per key, "the last registration wins", and the `registerAction` warning said in so many words "withdrawing package 'X' leaves the action with no handler". The pin tested that sentence of the warning.
- #31737 (`1cd0e0153e`) added the per-package slots (ADR-0150 D4). #32213 (`351c22c947`, ADR-0150 child B) rewrote the warning and dropped that clause. The same commit added the pin "Withdrawing one package leaves one owner: the call answers again" (it registers the remaining owner last, so it never reached the empty-key case). The old pin survived only because its arrangement registered the remaining owner first.
- ADR-0150 D5 says: "A bare address resolves while the name has one holder in the environment, and answers `409` with the candidates otherwise." With one holder left, "not found" contradicts D5. The hand-back gives D5's answer. So the old assertion pinned a stale consequence that D4 and D5 made into a bug, and the rewrite is right. Its CONTROL (no owner left, so "not found") keeps the empty case pinned.

**The hand-back holds ADR-0150 D5 in each remaining-holder case.** `unqualifiedHandler` counts owners from the package slots before it reads the unqualified slot (`engine-actions.ts:328-347`). So which entry the loop at `:479-484` restores never changes a refusal:
- *Two or more packages remain:* refused 409 naming them, as before the PR.
- *Object-less key, one package beside host code or a plugin:* refused 409, as before.
- *One package remains:* its handler runs. This is the card's shape.
- *Only the environment's handler remains:* it runs. The environment is never an owner, and this is what a restart answers.
- *A disabled package's handler is restored while an enabled owner remains:* the G4 path returns the enabled owner's handler (`:350-353`). With no enabled owner left, the door's disabled-package gate judges the call, as at boot.
- *Host code or a plugin beside one package on an object-bound key* (D5's "last registration" case): one of the two runs. Which one can differ from a restart; see N1.

### ② Semver level

- *`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right.* The PR adds the export `unbindAppArtifactHandlers` and the type `AppArtifactHandlerUnbinding`, and the moved answers turn a refusal (409 or "not found") into a served answer. Nothing that was accepted before is refused now. Every 409 that D5 rules stays a 409, because the count runs before the slot read. So no `!`, BREAKING paragraph or ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- *Patch for all three packages is right.* No authorable metadata moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` holds, and both lines start a line in the PR body and the changeset.
- **must-fix M1: the changeset's `Clause-②` line names one moved answer, and the engine change moves more.** `.changeset/33536-uninstall-unbinds-action-handlers.md:9` names only the bare call after an install-local uninstall, 409 → the remaining package's result. The objectql change at `engine-actions.ts:479-484` applies to every caller of `removeActionsByPackage`, and on `main` (`4bba8b8f`) these callers already reached the empty key:
  - the authored-action resync teardown, `ql.removeActionsByPackage('metadata-service')` (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:4566`). Deleting an environment-authored action whose key host code or a plugin also holds moves the bare call from "not found" to that handler.
  - the binder's re-bind teardown (`app-artifact-handlers.ts:342`). A re-install of a multi-package artifact that drops a body moves the bare call from "not found" to another package's handler under that key.
  - `ObjectQL#removePackage` (`packages/objectql/src/engine-compatibility-api.ts:264`), a public engine method, moves the same way.
  - the unqualified listing `listRegisteredActions()` now keeps the key after those removals. It feeds MCP `list_actions`' advertising probe (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:5472`), the script door's owner check (`:5692`) and the governance inventory (`plugin.ts:4470`). The action is therefore advertised again where it had disappeared.

  Each move is a widening and agrees with D5, so the value stays `yes (widening)`. But the declaration should name them. Add a sentence to the `Clause-②` line, and to the PR body, such as: "`ObjectQL#removeActionsByPackage` also hands the key back on every other removal: the authored-action resync, a re-bind that drops a package body, and `removePackage`. A bare call there moves from 'not found' to the one remaining holder's handler, and `listRegisteredActions()` keeps listing the key."

### ③ Boundary flags

- The diff stays in the three packages the area names. It adds one runtime barrel export and touches no `packages/spec`, ADR, generated file or protocol.
- *Dogfood battery.* It is not needed for a widening-only arm. At ACCEPT, re-read: the amended `Clause-②` line (M1); CI green, including `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which the PR could not measure locally; and the dogfood shards in the merge queue, which the PR declares as not measured.
- *Open, not in this PR.* `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` (protocol `deletePackage`) never calls an action, hook or function unbind. The leak there is read from the code, not reproduced. File it as its own card. The PR's own suggestion, `unbindAppArtifactHandlers` as a `runtime.package-handlers` uninstall cleanup, would close both doors at once, and adds a `cleanups` row that pins and dogfood read.

**Nits (none blocks).**
- N1. The hand-back picks "the last coordinate holding the key, in the order the slots were created" (`engine-actions.ts:482`). A slot is created the first time its coordinate registers any key, so this is not "the last registration of this key". The changeset (`:9`, "now answers what it answers after a restart") and the docblock (`engine.ts:1129-1134`) claim the restart answer. That holds for every refused case and for the card's shape. It can fail in one D5 case: host code beside one package on an object-bound key, when host code's slot was created earlier for another key but registered this key after the package. Then the hand-back runs the package's handler and a restart runs host code's. Either say "one remaining holder's handler" for that case, or keep a per-key registration sequence.
- N2. The hand-back adds a log warning to two tear-down-then-register paths that were silent before. When B re-binds beside A, the teardown hands the key to A, and B's re-registration then warns "second owner beside A" (`engine-actions.ts:176`). The same happens on each authored-action resync where an environment handler sits beside host code. This is log-only and does not change the accept set, but an upgrade now repeats the install's warning.
- N3. Three properties the review relies on have no pin, and no ablation covered them: (a) a refused withdrawal leaves the handlers bound (the `!withdrawal` guard at `:3705`); (b) a second `unbindAppArtifactHandlers` call is a no-op; (c) host code or an environment handler under the same key survives the unbind. A runtime unit case for (b) and (c) next to the binder's re-bind pins, plus a door case for (a) with `uninstallPackage` refusing, would cover them.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-E2-33536`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cyrFFk86Jqf7Mp5Rzw
Request: review · area E2 · head 32021b83094f4bdf06b1a8dc8e7ec467223c5828

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `32021b83094f4bdf06b1a8dc8e7ec467223c5828`
Local-runs: none

This reviews the delta on my FAIL at `793d8251` (record 6888444951).

Read: `793d8251..32021b83`, two commits with no rebase (`5c99acd4` docs(changeset), `32021b83` test). 4 files, +71/−15. The changes to `engine.ts` and `engine-actions.ts` are comment-only: the `removeActionsByPackage` docblock and the hand-back comment. No executable line changed. I re-read every caller of `removeActionsByPackage`, every reader of the unqualified `listRegisteredActions()` and the doors' handler-key rotation at this head. I ran nothing locally.

### ① Derived judgments

**The claims M1 asked for are true at the engine.**
- *The resync claim, and dropping "or a package", are right.* `resyncAuthoredActionsNow` filters `bindable` through `isArtifactShippedAction` (`plugin.ts:4560-4562`). That test is true for any registry holder's artifact at the owner key (`:3997-4011`). The exception is a declared `.custom` override, which `registerActionOverride` binds at the base's coordinate over the base's handler, so its teardown restores `beneath` and never empties the key. The teardown at `:4566` therefore empties a key only where host code or a plugin holds it. The re-registration loop after it is synchronous, so there is no window in which the key reads empty.
- *The re-bind (`app-artifact-handlers.ts:341-343`) and `removePackage` (`engine-compatibility-api.ts:264`)* reach the hand-back as named. A re-bind's own keys go back to the re-binder when they re-register, so only a dropped body leaves a lasting move, as the text says.
- *"Every 409 the bare-call rule answers stays a 409" is true.* `unqualifiedHandler` counts owners from the package slots and throws before it reads `this.actions` (`engine-actions.ts:328-349`).
- *The listing readers are correctly named.* MCP `list_actions`' probe (`action-execution.ts:5468-5484`) only widens: it advertises a key it had stopped advertising. The governance inventory (`plugin.ts:4470`) only warns. The script door's owner check (`:5692`) is the subject of M2.

**The new pins.**
- *(a) A refused withdrawal keeps the handlers bound* (`…-uninstall-handlers.test.ts:278`). It refuses at `registry.uninstallPackage` itself and asserts that the cleanups row shows the failure. It then checks that both holders are still there, that B's own call still runs, and that the bare call still answers 409 with both owners. It pins the `if (!withdrawal)` guard (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3705`), and the PR reports an ablation for it.
- *(b) A second unbind is a no-op* (`:296`). It is not ablated, but it is real for scoping. A second call that tore down beyond `app:B` would fail `holders()` → `[A]`, `call()` → `{ by: 'a' }`, or the hook count on `app:A` → `1`. It cannot tell whether the bind record was forgotten, because for a single-package artifact the recorded owners and the fallback owner are both `[app:B]`. That is acceptable: the forgetting is read in my prior ① and is harmless either way.
- *(c) Host code and the environment handler survive* (`:309`). It is not ablated, but it is real for scoping. An unbind that removed the host entry would make `call(B)` not found, because B has nothing of its own and the shared fallback would be gone. One that removed `metadata-service` would make `call('')` fail. It does not assert the bare call, which is fine.
- None of the three pins the guard except (a), which is the right split.

**N1's text is mostly right, with one gap (N4 below).** "One remaining holder's handler … in slot-creation order" matches the loop at `engine-actions.ts:479-484`.

### ② Semver level

- **must-fix M2: "a bare call moves from 'not found'" holds at `executeAction`, not at the doors the line names. At the doors, the before-state is often a fallback entry's handler, and a newly reached entry can bring a refusal.**
  - *The fallback.* Both doors dispatch through `executeRegisteredAction`. It walks `actionHandlerObjectKeys(objectName)` = `[OBJECT, 'global', '*']` × the declaration's handler-key candidates (`resolveActionHandlerKeys`: primary, target, name). On "not found" it moves to the next pair (`action-execution.ts:5428-5440`). Before this PR, a key that a resync, a re-bind or `removePackage` emptied did not answer "not found" at `POST /api/v1/actions/...` or MCP `run_action` whenever a later pair was held. The call then ran that pair's handler, for example `global:NAME`, or `OBJECT:<name>` behind a `target`. Now it runs the handed-back holder's handler. That is a different handler, not a refusal turned into an answer.
  - *The owner check moves with it.* `actionHandlerOwnerRefusal` judges the entry the dispatch reaches, from the same unqualified listing (`:5692`, `:5756`). Its owners are every other `script` declaration whose own rotation reaches that entry. When the entry moves, the owner set moves too, and it can gain a gated declaration.
  - *A concrete narrowing.* On `ticket`:
    - `ticket` is not P's object, and it declares `escalate`. Host code holds `ticket:escalate`, and package P registers it after host code. `ticket:escalate_urgent` and `global:escalate` are registered.
    - A declaration `escalate_urgent` on `ticket` (`target: 'escalate'`, `requiredPermissions: ['supervisor']`) has candidates `[escalate, escalate_urgent]`.
    - After `removePackage(P)` on `main`, a bare `escalate` call reaches `global:escalate`, and `escalate_urgent` reaches `ticket:escalate_urgent`. So `escalate_urgent` owns nothing the call runs, and the call is served.
    - At this head, the hand-back restores `ticket:escalate` to host code's entry. Both now reach `ticket:escalate`, and a non-supervisor's call is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (`:5766`). The same holds for an owner switched off in the activation ledger (409 `ACTION_DISABLED`, `:5777`).
    - When the handed-back entry is the environment's `metadata-service` entry, the hand-back can pick coordinate `''`, which test (c) sets up. With the plane unreadable, the call is refused 503 (`:5720`) where the fallback entry was served.
  - *Why this matters.* These are calls accepted before and refused after: a `(narrowing)` under AGENTS.md's closed pair, which is BREAKING. It is also what a restart answers, so the behaviour is defensible; the declaration is what is wrong. My record at `793d8251` said "nothing that was accepted before is refused now" and missed this rotation. I own that miss. The delta's new sentence states the before-state as "not found" for every caller, so the line now declares it wrongly.
  - *Fix, either way:*
    - (i) Keep `yes (widening)` and show the narrowing cannot occur. I do not see how, given the example.
    - (ii) Declare it. Use `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 marker and a migration line, or whatever disposition a seat rules for a restart-consistent narrowing. Name the before-state as "the next entry the door's rotation (`OBJECT` → `global` → `*`, per handler-key candidate) reaches; 'not found' only when none is held". Say that the owner gates of `actionHandlerOwnerRefusal` move with the entry, and can newly answer 403, 409 `ACTION_DISABLED` or 503. Make the same change in the PR body's "Every answer the engine hand-back moves" paragraph.
  - *Scope.* The reported install-local case is not affected. Before the PR, B's handler stayed bound, so the key never emptied there.
- Patch for all three packages still follows the kind: a non-protocol change. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- *Delta surface.* The delta changes tests, comments and the changeset only. It touches no spec, ADR or generated file.
- *N2* (the re-bind warning) is left to the Acceptance notes, as agreed.
- *N4 (nit).* The changeset says the slot-order choice "matters only where the bare-call rule runs one of two owners, host code or a plugin beside one package". It also matters with two shared owners and no package: host code beside a plugin, or two plugins. `unqualifiedHandler` refuses neither (`engine-actions.ts:345-349`), so the hand-back's slot order and a restart's last registration can differ there too. That is exactly the named resync case "whose key host code or a plugin also holds" when both do. Either widen the sentence or drop "only".
- *At ACCEPT.* Re-read the amended `Clause-②` line (M2), and check that CI is green, including `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:adr-0087-registration` if the arm becomes `(narrowing)`.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-E2-33536`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czXwx6JtQPvacrzzUw

**Seat ruling on review#3 M2 (6888764173): A.**

Keep the engine hand-back, and declare it as `yes (narrowing)`:
- add `!` to the title;
- add a BREAKING paragraph: after removePackage, after a re-bind that drops a body, and on the authored resync, an emptied unqualified key now resolves to the remaining holder's entry, so that owner's gates (403 / 409 ACTION_DISABLED / 503) can answer where the rotation used to fall through to a later entry. This is what a restart already answers;
- add the ADR-0087 marker, and correct the before-state wording.

The migration line says no data migration or heal. Nothing persisted changes (maintainer, 2026-11-14: no production customers yet). The install-local case the card reports is unaffected. A restart-consistent move is still a narrowing for the live process, so no separate disposition applies. review#3 re-reviews the declaration text only.

Request: review · area E2 · head 667a89f4d5d0b4a31a69afae35042a0b68188c61 · 2026-11-15T04:33Z

Text-only delta on FAIL 6888764173 (M2 + N4), under seat ruling A (6888779008); no executable source line changed. `32021b83..667a89f4`: the changeset now declares `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the `!`, a **BREAKING** paragraph, the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` and a no-migration line, and drops "only" from the slot-order caveat (two shared owners). The PR title carries the `!`, and the body has the corrected before-state, the three paths and the install-local note. One added pin, in `packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts`: after the hand-back the door runs host code's entry instead of `global:approve`, and the gated owner answers 403. Its ablation (hand-back disabled, objectql rebuilt) reds with `expected 'global' to be 'host'`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `667a89f4d5d0b4a31a69afae35042a0b68188c61`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-uninstall-handlers.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/bound-action-collision-report.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-actions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts + packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-compatibility-api.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (cited, read, not reviewed)

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, judged against the spec and ADRs on `main`, makes the spec's own gates real; it takes away no declared capability. ADR-0066 D4 and ADR-0110 D2 (`actionHandlerOwnerRefusal`'s docblock) say a call is judged by the owners of the handler entry its dispatch reaches. Before this PR, after a live removal, the door fell through to a later entry that a restart of the same tree would not reach. That let a caller run past an owner's `requiredPermissions` or activation switch while the process lived, and be refused after a restart. The hand-back closes that live-vs-boot divergence: the newly refused calls are ones the boot state already refuses. The narrowing stays inside the three named removal paths, and the package-qualified call reads its own slot, so it is untouched. Choosing to keep the hand-back and declare it (ruling A) over reverting it is sound: reverting would leave the engine's bare `executeAction` answering "not found" for an action a remaining owner holds. No must-fix or should-fix. N5 is a nit.
